players.note: Tyler Shough might have crapped the bed from a real-life standpoint last week, but he has continued to cook from a fantasy standpoint as the QB3 in fantasy points per game. The only quarterbacks with more fantasy points per game than Shough this season are Josh Allen and Brock Purdy. Wild. Among 31 qualifying passers, Shough is 11th in passing success rate, 13th in highly accurate throw rate, and third in hero throw rate. Shough should still rack up the stats this week, but it won't be easy. Atlanta has allowed the eighth-fewest yards per attempt, the sixth-lowest passing success rate, and the 14th-fewest EPA per dropback. Atlanta also has the second-best pressure rate and the fifth-best quick pressure rate. Shough has navigated pressure well this season with the ninth-best yards per attempt and the fifth-best passing success rate against pressure.

Dak Prescott is the QB8 in fantasy points per game. Among 31 qualifying quarterbacks, Prescott is eighth in passing success rate, second in highly accurate throw rate, seventh in catchable target rate, and he has the ninth-lowest off-target rate. Prescott is also 13th in fantasy points per dropback. Prescott should turn in another QB1 performance this week against a struggling Houston pass defense. The Texans have allowed the seventh-highest yards per attempt, the eighth-highest passer rating, and the third-highest CPOE. Prescott should have clean pockets against a pass defense that surprisingly has the second-lowest pressure rate and the fifth-lowest quick pressure rate.

Well, I was worried about it. Bryce Young finally came back to earth last week as the QB22 for fantasy. Young's deeper metrics made me worry about this, and they don't look any better after Week 3. Among 31 qualifying passers, he's seventh in yards per attempt, ninth in hero throw rate, and has the fourth-highest deep ball rate, but he also has the fourth-lowest highly accurate throw rate, the lowest catchable target rate, and the ninth-highest off-target rate. Young is attempting to walk a weekly tightrope of a volatile but high-upside deep-ball passer. There will be boom weeks and big-time down weeks if he continues to live in this world all season. Luckily for Young, the Lions are a very accommodating opponent for this style of play and should allow for a bounce back this week. Detroit has allowed the ninth-most yards per attempt, the third-highest passing success rate, and the sixth-highest CPOE. The Lions have also struggled with defending the deep ball, giving up the fourth-highest deep ball completion rate and passing success rate downfield.

Well, Kyler Murray's first game as Minny's starter didn't go great. He was the QB27 in weekly scoring last week. Yes, I know Justin Jefferson got banged up last week, which no doubt impacted Murray's day. That doesn't mean that we can excuse his performance. After last week, among 38 qualifying passers, Murray has the third-lowest yards per attempt, the lowest passing success rate, the lowest highly accurate throw rate, and the fourth-lowest catchable target rate. WOOF! Murray also ran only twice for 17 yards. None of this will get the job done, but maybe Miami is the magic elixir for Murray in Week 4. Miami has allowed the second-most yards per attempt, the fourth-highest passer rating, the highest passing success rate, and the most fantasy points per dropback to quarterbacks. Murray could look revitalized for at least one week.

C.J. Stroud is the QB15 in fantasy points per game, but he has been struggling as a passer to begin the 2026 season. Among 31 qualifying passers, Stroud has the tenth-fewest yards per attempt, the 12th-lowest passing success rate, the tenth-lowest catchable target rate, and the fifth-fewest fantasy points per dropback. Stroud has further proven so far that his rookie season is the outlier in his NFL resume. As bad as Stroud has been, Dallas might prop him up this week. Stroud could post solid QB2 numbers this week against Dallas's underwhelming pass defense. Dallas has allowed the 12th-most yards per attempt and the second-highest EPA per dropback and passing success rate.

After his bellyflop in Week 1, Matthew Stafford has been a strong QB1 with QB6 and QB9 finishes in weekly scoring. Since Week 2, among 28 qualifying passers, Stafford ranks fifth in yards per attempt, seventh in fantasy points per dropback, 17th in highly accurate throw rate, and 15th in catchable target rate. Stafford could post QB1 numbers again this week against an up-and-down Philly pass defense. Philly has allowed the 11th-fewest yards per attempt and the tenth-lowest passing success rate, but they have also surrendered the eighth-most EPA per dropback and rank 18th in CPOE permitted. Philly has the sixth-lowest pressure rate this season, so Stafford should have time in the pocket to find the holes in the Eagles' coverage.

Jordan Love is the QB17 in fantasy points per game with one QB1 (QB11) outing in weekly scoring this season. Love has been rattled all season behind his patchwork offensive line, which the Packers are attempting to band-aid together after signing nearly every free-agent offensive-line option with a pulse this week. Among 31 qualifying passers, Love has the fourth-lowest passing success rate, the 11th-lowest yards per attempt, the lowest highly accurate throw rate, and the second-highest off-target rate. I'm not saying that Love will be amazing this week, but the Bucs pass defense isn't one that I fear. Their season-long metrics are being propped up by the fact that they have faced Deshaun Watson and Kyler Murray over the last two weeks. Yes, they have allowed the 13th-lowest CPOE, the 12th-fewest fantasy points per dropback, and the 13th-lowest EPA per dropback, but again they have faced Watson and Murray in two of three games in this sample. The Bucs also have the fourth-lowest pressure rate and the 11th-lowest quick pressure rate. If the new additions to the Green Bay line can help buy Love any more time this week, he could surprise.

Bo Nix has looked like a backup quarterback for most of the season. It has been tough to watch. Among 31 qualifying passers, Nix has the ninth-fewest yards per attempt, the sixth-lowest passing success rate, the tenth-lowest highly accurate throw rate, the seventh-lowest catchable target rate, and the third-highest turnover-worthy throw rate. Yep, it has been THAT BAD. I don't see Nix turning it around this week. The 49ers have allowed the seventh-fewest yards per attempt, the 11th-lowest CPOE, and the third-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

Drake Maye has looked like a turnover-prone shell of his 2025 self to begin this season as the QB36 in fantasy points per game. Among 31 qualifying passers, Maye has the sixth-lowest passing success rate and the highest turnover-worthy throw rate while ranking 16th in highly accurate throw rate and 17th in catchable target rate. He also hasn't run enough weekly to save his fantasy value, with more than 20 rushing yards in only one game. Maybe this is the "get right" spot for Maye, but at this point I gotta see it to believe it. Buffalo has allowed the 11th-most yards per attempt, the seventh-highest passing success rate, and the 11th-highest CPOE.

Last week, Marcus Mariota surprised everyone as the QB13 for the week, as he was highly efficient with three passing scores against Seattle. Mariota added only five rushing attempts and 11 yards on the ground. Among 31 qualifying passers this season, Mariota is seventh-best in passing success rate, sixth in passer rating, eighth in catchable target rate, and first in hero throw rate. I expect him to add more rushing this season as Washington's starter. Mariota could flirt with QB1 production again this week against a pass defense that has allowed the fifth-most EPA per dropback, the third-most yards per attempt, and the eighth-highest passing success rate. Jayden Daniels returned to practice this week, but I would be shocked if he played this week.

Last week, in his first game back, Sam Darnold was forced to air it out, and he finished as the QB2 for the week. Darnold finished with 379 passing yards and four passing touchdowns (two picks). Among 38 qualifying passers, he ranks sixth in yards per attempt, 13th in passing success rate, 26th in highly accurate throw rate, fourth in catchable target rate, and seventh in fantasy points per dropback. Darnold should follow it up with another solid fantasy showing against a Bolts pass defense that has allowed the seventh-most yards per attempt, the fifth-highest passing success rate, and the ninth-most EPA per dropback.

Jacoby Brissett is the QB20 in fantasy points per game with a QB4 performance in weekly scoring last week. Among 31 qualifying passers, he has been a quick-passing point guard with the lowest time to throw, the fourth-lowest aDOT, and the third-fewest yards per attempt. Brissett also has the fourth-fewest fantasy points per dropback while ranking 13th in passing success rate. Brissett should have another strong QB2 performance with the upside to flirt with QB1 production this week. New York has allowed the 14th-highest passing success rate, the seventh-highest CPOE, the tenth-most fantasy points per dropback, and the sixth-most EPA per dropback.

Daniel Jones has struggled to open the season as the QB34 in fantasy points per game. Jones hasn't eclipsed 13 fantasy points in any start this season. Among 31 qualifying passers, Jones has the sixth-fewest yards per attempt, the 14th-lowest passing success rate, the fourth-lowest CPOE, the fifth-lowest aDOT, and the 12th-highest off-target rate. Jones has been BAD. I don't have a ton of faith in Jones, but the matchup is glorious this week. Maybe he flashes a fantasy pulse this week as a decent QB2. Washington has allowed the fifth-most yards per attempt, the most passing touchdowns, the sixth-highest passing success rate, and the fourth-most EPA per dropback.

Geno Smith is the QB19 in fantasy points per game after last week's fantasy point explosion as the QB3 for the week. Smith has had a mini renaissance to begin this season. Among 31 qualifying passers, he is eighth in yards per attempt, tenth in passing success rate, second in catchable target rate, and 11th in hero throw rate. The Bears look like a tough assignment on paper, but through three games they got lit up by Bryce Young and then had good outings against Carson Wentz and a struggling Jalen Hurts. I'm not scared of this pass defense despite allowing the ninth-lowest passing success rate, the seventh-fewest EPA per dropback, and the fifth-lowest CPOE. Chicago has the tenth-lowest pressure rate. I expect Smith to have time to pick apart this pass defense in Week 4. Smith is a solid QB2 who could flirt with QB1 production again this week.

Justin Herbert and the Chargers offense have been one of the biggest disappointments through three games. Herbert is the QB32 in fantasy points per game without a single game with more than 15 fantasy points. Among 31 qualifying passers, Herbert has the 14th-fewest yards per attempt, the seventh-fewest fantasy points per dropback, the eighth-lowest passing success rate, and the fifth-lowest EPA per dropback. I don't see this being the week that Herbert turns things around against this vaunted Seattle pass defense. Seattle has allowed the fewest yards per attempt, the seventh-lowest passing success rate, and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

In his first game back under center, Michael Penix was the QB20 in fantasy. Among 30 qualifying quarterbacks last week, he was third in yards per attempt, 12th in passing success rate, and 13th in catchable target rate while having the third-lowest aDOT (6.41). Penix should have another solid starting outing in Week 4 against a Saints pass defense that has allowed the ninth-highest passer rating, the fourth-highest passing success rate, and the 12th-most EPA per dropback. Penix should have clean pockets to work from, as the Saints have the ninth-lowest pressure rate and the 12th-lowest quick pressure rate.

Kirko Chainz has the Raiders undefeated as the QB11 in fantasy points per game. Yes, I'm as surprised as you are by that last statement. Cousins has been playing good football. Among 31 qualifying passers, he ranks 16th in yards per attempt, 14th in passing success rate, 18th in highly accurate throw rate, and ninth in catchable target rate. He'll have his hands full with a surprisingly stout Chiefs' pass defense. Kansas City has allowed the third-fewest yards per attempt, the fourth-lowest passing success rate, and the fourth-lowest CPOE. While Spags has been in his bag with the coverages, he has only been able to muster the 15th-best quick pressure rate while standing at 13th-best in pressure rate. Cousins will have to operate quickly with the ball in his hands this week.

In weekly fantasy scoring, Deshaun Watson has finished as the QB21, QB12, and QB14. Watson has added some rushing equity with eight rushing attempts and 35 yards on the ground per game. He has continued to struggle as a passer, as a low aDOT point guard. Among 31 qualifying passers, Watson has the second-lowest aDOT, the 14th-lowest catchable target rate, the eighth-highest off-target rate, and the fifth-highest turnover-worthy throw rate. Watson has the fourth-highest percentage of his passing yards that have come from YAC (59.1%). Watson could have another passable QB2 week against a Steelers pass defense that has allowed the tenth-most yards per attempt, the 11th-highest passing success rate, and the ninth-highest CPOE.

Ben Johnson hasn't "officially" named a starting quarterback for Week 4, but all indications are pointing in the direction of Tyson Bagent. Bagent will be making his first start for Chicago with Ben Johnson as his head coach. Against Minnesota, Bagent came in for Caleb Williams and had nine passing attempts. He completed five of them with 6.0 yards per attempt, but I'm not taking anything away from that abbreviated performance. In the preseason, Bagent was wonderful, ranking fourth in yards per attempt and 12th in adjusted completion rate among 70 qualifying passers (per PFF). Bagent has a middle-of-the-road matchup this week against the Jets, who have allowed the 12th-highest passing success rate while ranking 18th in CPOE and EPA per dropback. He will have to make quick decisions against a defense that has the 14th-best pressure rate and ranks first in quick pressure. Bagent is a QB2 with upside.

The falloff had to come at some point, but it appears here for Jameis Winston. Over the last two games, he has been the QB32 and QB31 in weekly fantasy scoring. I think it's just a matter of time before we see JJ McCarthy making starts for the Giants. Among 31 qualifying passers, Winston has the lowest yards per attempt, the lowest passing success rate, the fifth-lowest highly accurate throw rate, and the fourth-lowest catchable target rate. I'm not playing Winston. I don't care about the matchup.

Aaron Rodgers had a mini renaissance last week as the QB7 in fantasy. Overall, he is the QB27 in fantasy points per game, with only that performance as his claim to fantasy fame for 2026 as a QB1. Among 31 qualifying quarterbacks, Rodgers has the fifth-lowest yards per attempt, the 11th-lowest passing success rate, the sixth-lowest catchable target rate, and the 12th-lowest hero throw rate. Rodgers will likely return to the QB2 ranks this week against a pass defense that has allowed the 13th-fewest yards per attempt while ranking 16th in passing success rate and EPA per dropback allowed. The key for Cleveland this week is for their pass rush, which is third in pressure rate and fourth in quick pressure rate, to get home. If it does, Rodgers will have trouble, as he has the 12th-fewest yards per attempt and the tenth-lowest passing success rate when under pressure this season.

With Baker Mayfield out, Jalon Daniels will draw the start for the Bucs this week. The dual-threat rookie has some rushing upside, with at least 404 rushing yards and four scores on the ground in each of his final three collegiate seasons. My comp for him as a prospect was Tyler Huntley. He could provide similar output as the Bucs starter. During the preseason, Daniels ran 14 times, churning out 37 rushing yards. Among 70 qualifying passers in the preseason, he was only 48th in yards per attempt, 30th in adjusted completion rate, and 37th in big-time throw rate (per PFF). During his final collegiate season, among all FBS quarterbacks with at least 150 dropbacks, Daniels was 76th in adjusted completion rate, 40th in yards per attempt, and 33rd in big-time throw rate. Daniels could return decent QB2 production this week if he does utilize his legs in the rushing department. The Packers are a middle-of-the-road pass defense, ranking 17th in CPOE, 16th in fantasy points per dropback, and allowing the 14th-most yards per attempt.

Through three games this season, Malik Willis has finished as the QB13, QB22, and QB28 in weekly fantasy scoring. In two of those games, he has been rushing like we hoped, averaging 7.5 rushing attempts and 47.5 rushing yards. Willis hasn't been great as a passer despite flashing his arm talent at times. Among 31 qualifying passers, he ranks 13th in yards per attempt and sixth in hero throw rate, but he also has the fifth-lowest catchable target rate and the third-highest off-target rate. Willis will need all the rushing equity he can get this week to save his fantasy day. Minnesota's defense has been nasty. They have allowed the fourth-fewest passing touchdowns, the lowest passer rating, and the lowest passing success rate. The Vikings also have the sixth-best pressure rate and the ninth-best quick pressure rate. Good luck, Willis.

Cam Ward has been a miserable disappointment this season as the QB27 in fantasy points per game. I was worried about Ward this preseason as the all-22 film scared the crap out of me. Nothing Ward has done in the regular season has made me feel any better. Among 31 qualifying passers, Ward has the fourth-fewest yards per attempt, the ninth-lowest CPOE and passing success rate, the second-lowest highly accurate throw rate, and the eighth-highest turnover-worthy throw rate. I don't see Ward turning his season around this week. Baltimore has allowed the ninth-fewest yards per attempt, the 13th-lowest passing success rate, and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per dropback. Ward is a sit weekly until he shows some glimmer of hope.
